properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured), limitation 11, ALREADY RECORDED as this requirement: `reflow2 init --harness vscode` knows VS Code only as an MCP client. It writes .vscode/mcp.json (git-ignored) and an AGENTS.md saying reflow2 is "reached through the reflow2 MCP server, already configured in this repo". There is no door harness and no .github/instructions/ or .github/hooks/ file, and nothing mentions --call. So the door setup can only be a hand-written user file that update cannot see
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), triage agent D, on limitation 11 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02 ("The setup is one person's local file; reflow2 init / update don't install or refresh it"), and idea 1.

② PRECEDENT: this requirement (step 5 of epoch:planned-the-call-door-works-for-an-agent-that-cannot-use-mcp) and the settled dec:idea-the-call-door-becomes-a-supported-harness-for-an-agent-that-cannot-use-mcp already hold the remedy. Linked, not re-minted.

⑤ MEASURED. main's tools/ and getting-started/ were extracted from origin/main 66620f7 into a scratch kit. `python3 kit/tools/reflow2_init.py <scratch>/initproj --harness vscode --binary <0.77.0>` ran with an isolated HOME. The project held a pre-existing .github/copilot-instructions.md. Log: /home/ajs7/.claude/jobs/fa666a94/tmp/triage-D/l11-init-vscode.log.
- Files written: AGENTS.md; .vscode/mcp.json (servers.reflow2 = binary --graph-path .reflow2/graph --export-to docs/design/initproj.json --shared); one marked pointer line appended to .github/copilot-instructions.md; .gitignore; .gitattributes; docs/design/initproj.json; .reflow2/kit-version.json {"harnesses":["vscode"]}.
- Printed: "loop nudge NOT INSTALLED — reflow2 has no hook for vscode".
- .gitignore lists .vscode/mcp.json ("they carry an absolute path to YOUR binary"). So even the MCP route's file is per-person.
- AGENTS.md line 9: "It is reached through the **`reflow2` MCP server**, already configured in this repo." That is false where the organisation blocks third-party MCP. No line in it mentions --call.
- The harness switch exists: --harness takes claude, opencode, grok and vscode, with copilot as an alias for claude. Every entry is an MCP config generator (MCP_CONFIGS). Nothing is written to .github/instructions/ or .github/hooks/, and no harness value means "the door".
- `reflow2 update` is the same script with --update (the wrapper exec's reflow2_init.py --update, reflow2_install.py:428). So update can refresh only what init knows how to write.

⑥ CLASS: a route nobody installs is a route nobody can update. reflow2's install path models a harness as "which MCP config file", so a harness with MCP blocked has no row to hang the door's instructions, skill stubs or hooks on. The requirement's MUST covers instructions, skill stubs, attribution and a CI probe. WHAT THE REPORT ADDS (idea 1 with idea 12): the same harness should also write VS Code hook files (.github/hooks/*.json). Those are open in dec:idea-how-reflow2-triggers-the-loop-for-a-call-door-agent-in-vs-code. One further point the requirement does not name: the AGENTS.md pointer init writes for vscode states the MCP route as fact, so a door harness must change that sentence too.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a door harness should replace the vscode MCP entry or sit beside it. A team with some members on MCP and some on the door is plausible, and that choice is the owner's.
